gen_risks.description: The UK ETS carbon price is currently too low to incentivize CCUS deployment without subsidy, making emitting carbon cheaper than capturing and storing it.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide long-term business model subsidy contracts (such as 15-year CfD-style strike price agreements) to bridge the financial gap between carbon market prices and capture costs.
gen_risks.evidence: The Carbon Price is currently too low to incentivise deployment, there is a first-mover disadvantage due to high start-up costs

gen_risks.description: CO2 could leak from deep geological storage reservoirs or transportation pipelines, causing environmental damage and financial liabilities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Underwrite low-probability, high-impact leakage risks via the Supplementary Compensation Agreement (SCA) and maintain extensive offshore sentinel and monitoring wells.
gen_risks.evidence: government will underwrite several key high-impact, low-probability risks – principally relating to CO2 leakage – via the Supplementary Compensation Agreement (SCA).

gen_risks.description: Sequential FID timeline across anchor and build-out projects risks T&S network underutilisation if build-out capture projects are delayed or fail to reach FID.
gen_risks.mitigation: Include uncertain cost reopeners in the economic licence to disallow T&S CapEx for uncommitted projects, while filling excess capacity through the HyNet top-up process.
gen_risks.evidence: This incremental approach... introduces a risk of network underutilisation and revenue support exposure

gen_risks.description: Complex cross-chain technical interdependencies between T&S network operations and capture projects could lead to cascading operational outages or stranded volume risks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish the DESNZ Cluster Sponsor Function to actively manage cross-chain delivery risks and coordinate outage schedules with Ofgem and LCCC.
gen_risks.evidence: In addition, HMG covers some of the ‘cross-chain’ risks from the interdependencies between the T&SCo and capture projects.

gen_risks.description: Construction capital expenditure overruns on the T&S network could increase overall infrastructure costs and funding requirements.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce a 40/60 cost sharing factor within the RAB economic licence model, ensuring the T&SCo only recoups 40% of CapEx incurred above agreed allowances.
gen_risks.evidence: Eni T&S network construction overruns... the T&SCo will only recoup 40% of any costs in excess of the agreed level.

gen_risks.description: Decommissioning costs for offshore platforms, wells, and pipelines at end-of-life could exceed accumulated funds, creating a financial deficit.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce mandatory financial security requirements through NSTA and OPRED regulations and execute formal Decommissioning Shortfall Agreements.
gen_risks.evidence: Decommissioning fund shortfall... NSTA and Opred requirements for financial security

gen_risks.description: Exchequer exposure reaching pre-defined financial caps could trigger Secretary of State rights to discontinue T&S network support, stranding assets.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement rigorous monthly budget control and monitoring across DESNZ, LCCC, and Ofgem to track cumulative subsidy drawdown against thresholds.
gen_risks.evidence: Discontinuation Agreement... if support provided reaches a defined threshold, DESNZ SoS has the right to discontinue the T&S network.

gen_risks.description: Delays in passing FID-critical secondary legislation or finalizing the CCS Network Code before contract execution could delay project financial close.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prioritise FID-critical secondary legislation through dedicated parliamentary schedules and conduct pre-referral engagement on the full-form CCS Network Code.
gen_risks.evidence: A number of activities are still ongoing to achieve FID including stage 3 negotiations... FID critical secondary legislation

gen_risks.description: Global supply chain constraints and inflation could cause capital cost increases and force re-negotiation of time-limited supplier bids if FID is delayed.
gen_risks.mitigation: Progress anchor projects to FID expeditiously to secure time-limited supplier bids and perform continuous cost and procurement assurance.
gen_risks.evidence: Reopening the supplier bids would be a dynamic scenario... underlying costs are expected to increase.

gen_risks.description: Hard-to-abate UK industrial emitters could suffer carbon leakage by relocating manufacturing abroad if decarbonisation costs remain uncompetitive.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide predictable 15-year business model revenue support and upfront capital co-funding through the CIF and NZHF to preserve UK industrial competitiveness.
gen_risks.evidence: manufacturers of critical industrial materials may relocate to more favourable jurisdictions due to the escalating costs of emissions; otherwise known as ‘carbon leakage’.

gen_risks.description: Key delivery and regulatory partner organisations (such as Ofgem, LCCC, and CGL) may lack sufficient resourcing or capability post-FID to oversee complex contracts.
gen_risks.mitigation: Require partner organisations to complete formal Organisational Readiness Statements and deploy specialized technical, legal, and PMO advisory support.
gen_risks.evidence: Partner organisations’ capacity and capability... partner organisations with significant responsibility to complete Organisational Readiness Statements.

gen_risks.description: Local public or community opposition regarding CO2 infrastructure, compression, and pipeline routing could cause planning delays and public resistance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Proactively engage local communities, share best practices through the CCUS Council, and partner with Arm's Length Bodies to demonstrate safety.
gen_risks.evidence: Testing has shown awareness of CCUS is growing but with many still undecided of their view.

gen_risks.description: Withdrawal or insolvency of individual anchor or build-out emitters (e.g. EETH or Protos) could breach volume assumptions and increase unit costs for remaining network users.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct rigorous corporate financial due diligence prior to FID and execute the HyNet top-up process to recruit replacement CO2 volume producers.
gen_risks.evidence: Discontinuation risk for EETH and Protos... BLN0 has requested to withdraw from the CCUS sequencing process

gen_risks.description: Proposed subsidy structures or capital grant distributions could face legal challenge or adverse assessment under the UK Subsidy Control Act 2022.
gen_risks.mitigation: Submit formal subsidy assessments to the Subsidy Advice Unit (SAU) at least 3 months prior to FID and conduct thorough pre-referral alignment with DBT.
gen_risks.evidence: Subsidy controls and other legal requirements... assessment of each subsidy scheme will be submitted by DESNZ to the Subsidy Advice Unit

gen_risks.description: Operational fraud or misrepresentation in grant funding claims (CIF/NZHF) or ongoing revenue support payments could result in exchequer financial loss.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy the DESNZ Central Grants and Loans (CGL) team and LCCC to enforce strict claim verification, audit rights, and compliance checks under Grant Funding Agreements.
gen_risks.evidence: Fraud... Central Grants and Loans (CGL) Team will be the delivery partner for all grants awarded.

gt_risks.description: There is a risk that government (HMG) is exposed to increased costs for Track-1 post-Financial Investment Decision (FID), and that cost pressures are unaffordable within delegated budgets. [Strategic Case risk T1SR1, Section 2.5 'Identify high level potential risks', p.20-21; source rating: High/Possible.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Contractual mechanisms ensure HMG only takes on specific risks where appropriate, with liability limited and counterparties incentivised to control costs; governance mechanisms monitor costs and provide early warning of overruns; contingent liability exposure is accurately monitored.

gt_risks.description: There is a risk that the programme does not realise its intended benefits for Track-1. [Strategic Case risk T1SR3, Section 2.5, p.20-21; source rating: High/Possible.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Projects undergo detailed technical assurance and financial due diligence; projects must meet Initial Conditions Precedent (ICPs) before contracts take effect and Operational CPs thereafter, with LCCC able to terminate and avoid paying for an underperforming project; contractual mechanisms allocate performance-related risk to the private sector; continued engagement with the global Carbon Management Challenge to expand CCUS use and deliver UK trade benefits.

gt_risks.description: There is a risk that the post-FID operating model across public and private sector parties will not operate successfully. [Strategic Case risk T1SR4, Section 2.5, p.20-21; source rating: Medium/Possible.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Progress of arm's-length bodies' (ALBs') capacity (funding, resource) and capability (knowledge, skills) to operate successfully post-FID is monitored through the Delivery Board; a DESNZ Cluster Sponsor Function will be set up between FID and Commercial Operations Date (COD) to mitigate risks to cluster delivery and system integration; readiness-testing mechanisms are in place ahead of FID; FY24/25 funding for the ALBs to fulfil their roles has been secured.

gt_risks.description: There is a risk of an unclear exit path for HMG from its role in the Track-1 commercial framework. [Strategic Case risk T1SR5, Section 2.5, p.20-21; source rating: High/Possible.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Key planned developments include amendments to the process for granting economic licences, a move toward a competitive allocation process for capture contracts, and evolution of transport & storage business models to reflect an increased private-sector role in managing cross-chain risks; cost-reduction levers (UK ETS pricing, CBAMs) are intended to help cultivate a self-sustaining industry and enable an HMG exit path.
